frames.label: To create internal dents in a tube, place it in a die that contains the desired indent features and apply internal hy...
frames.main_point: To create internal dents in a tube, place it in a die that contains the desired indent features and apply internal hydraulic pressure (using oil or water) to force the tube wall into the mold cavities.
frames.source_quote: Fit it into a mold which has the indents correctly placed and then pressurize the inside - hydraulic pressure with oil or water may be used.
frames.subject: tube hydroforming using an external mold and internal hydraulic pressure
frames.thread_title: Best way to dent a pipe from the inside?

frames.label: Applying the internal pressure as a pulse can be more effective than increasing it gradually when forming dents with...
frames.main_point: Applying the internal pressure as a pulse can be more effective than increasing it gradually when forming dents with hydraulic pressurization.
frames.source_quote: A pulse may be effective for this as opposed to a gradual increase in pressure.
frames.subject: pressure pulsing versus gradual pressurization in hydroforming
frames.thread_title: Best way to dent a pipe from the inside?

frames.label: A dedicated three-part jig enables producing the same internal pipe dent consistently across multiple parts, improvin...
frames.main_point: A dedicated three-part jig enables producing the same internal pipe dent consistently across multiple parts, improving repeatability.
frames.source_quote: This is a three part precise jig that can repeat the process many times.
frames.subject: three-part jig for repeatable pipe denting
frames.thread_title: Best way to dent a pipe from the inside?

frames.label: Before applying the forming force, strap stainless steel belts above and below the target area to confine deformation...
frames.main_point: Before applying the forming force, strap stainless steel belts above and below the target area to confine deformation and prevent the tube from bulging outside the intended dent zone.
frames.source_quote: you secure the indentation spot with stainless steel belts upside and downside of the spot to be dented, not to let it bulge outside the desired zone
frames.subject: strapping to constrain bulging during denting
frames.thread_title: Best way to dent a pipe from the inside?

frames.label: The die set comprises left/right solid supports with a round notch that guide and support a moving quarter-circle ham...
frames.main_point: The die set comprises left/right solid supports with a round notch that guide and support a moving quarter-circle hammer to create the dent.
frames.source_quote: there are left and right solid pipes with a round notch to support the  moving quarter circle hammer shown in black.
frames.subject: round-notch supports with quarter-circle hammer

frames.label: When executed properly, brazed joints can be nearly as strong as welded joints
frames.main_point: When executed properly, brazed joints can be nearly as strong as welded joints.
frames.source_quote: Brazing is a very strong joint if done properly (nearly as good as welding).
frames.subject: brazed joint strength vs welding
frames.thread_title: Joining bronze gear to bronze shaft

frames.label: For mass-produced probe tips that are indeed single-piece, they are probably made by non-machining methods such as ex...
frames.main_point: For mass-produced probe tips that are indeed single-piece, they are probably made by non-machining methods such as extrusion or forming rather than machining.
frames.source_quote: If the mass produced tips you saw are indeed single-piece then they are probably made with non-machining methods such as extrusions and forming which don't even fall under the purview of "machining".
frames.subject: manufacturing methods for single-piece probe tips

frames.label: Some thermocouple probe tips that may look monolithic are actually brazed onto the tube
frames.main_point: Some thermocouple probe tips that may look monolithic are actually brazed onto the tube. Visual inspection can reveal a brazed joint.
frames.source_quote: Because I am holding a couple of thermocouple probes in my hand right now and the tip is clearly brazed on.
frames.subject: brazed tips on thermocouple probes

frames.label: Recommend a shrink fit for this case: it will not come out, provides flexibility to shape the head to purpose, is ach...
frames.main_point: Recommend a shrink fit for this case: it will not come out, provides flexibility to shape the head to purpose, is achievable in a typical machine shop without special machines, and requires careful tolerances.
frames.source_quote: In your case I would just recommend a good shrink fit. It's never going to come out and you get more flexibility to make the head more suited to purpose. This should be well within reach of a machine shop and doesn't need crazy custom machines. It just needs careful tolerances.
frames.subject: shrink fitting a tip onto a tube

frames.label: Finish grinding and polishing can hide the joint line of a brazed or shrink-fit tip so it appears seamless, with colo...
frames.main_point: Finish grinding and polishing can hide the joint line of a brazed or shrink-fit tip so it appears seamless, with color potentially the only visible clue if dissimilar materials are used.
frames.source_quote: And with appropriate finish grinding and polishing you won't even be able to see the seam line (apart from colour should you choose a different material).
frames.subject: seam concealment by finish grinding and polishing

frames.label: Form the tapered tip by spin forming the stainless tube on a lathe to the desired profile
frames.main_point: Form the tapered tip by spin forming the stainless tube on a lathe to the desired profile. This achieves most of the geometry before any sealing or finishing.
frames.source_quote: If you start with a stainless steel tube and spin form it on a lathe to the right profile you're 95% of the way there.
frames.subject: spin forming tube tip on lathe

frames.label: Seal the hollow end by using heat to fuse the tip closed or by applying a brazing or soldering process
frames.main_point: Seal the hollow end by using heat to fuse the tip closed or by applying a brazing or soldering process. Expect to experiment to dial in the method for your tube and profile.
frames.source_quote: Some experimentation might be required, but you can likely use heat to melt the tip and seal it. Or perhaps some kind of brazing or solder.
frames.subject: sealing hollow tube tip by fusing or brazing/soldering

frames.label: Choose finishing based on how cleanly the tip was sealed
frames.main_point: Choose finishing based on how cleanly the tip was sealed. A precise seal may only need a quick polish, while a less precise seal may require a final machining pass.
frames.source_quote: Depending on how precise the sealing method is, you might only need a quick polish to clean it up, or maybe a final machining step.
frames.subject: finishing operations after sealing tube tip

frames.label: When measuring a violin, use an indicator probe with a plastic ball (Delrin or PTFE) rather than the usual carbide tip
frames.main_point: When measuring a violin, use an indicator probe with a plastic ball (Delrin or PTFE) rather than the usual carbide tip. This tip choice is recommended for this delicate application.
frames.source_quote: For either type, for a violin, you will want to get a probe with a plastic ball such as delrin or teflon, and not the carbide that usually come with either type of indicator.
frames.subject: indicator probe tip material selection for delicate surfaces
